questionsRewritten.cx-growth-rates-q8: Replace former repetitive calculation or terse recall feedback with a self-contained conceptual walkthrough. Independently checked focus: Measure the input in bits. A prime forces the loop to try every candidate divisor below its value. Adding bits greatly increases that value, so a linear iteration count in numeric value is exponential in bit length. Early exits on composites do not remove the prime-input worst case; large-integer division adds further cost.
questionsRewritten.cx-growth-rates-q9: Replace numerical crossover solving with interpretation of constants and representative benchmarks. Independently checked focus: Separate current input bounds from eventual growth. A simple implementation may have less setup, allocation and per-step overhead. questionsRewritten.cx-growth-rates-q11: Replace former repetitive calculation or terse recall feedback with a self-contained conceptual walkthrough. Independently checked focus: The filter visits pixels, not just rows. Doubling width doubles pixels per row; doubling height doubles the number of rows. That gives four times the work if per-pixel cost stays comparable. A linear algorithm still takes longer when its input grows.

questionsRewritten.cx-asymptotic-notation-q4: Replace arithmetic trials of constants with diagnosis of valid upper-bound proof obligations. Independently checked focus: A valid bound has two fixed choices: multiplier and starting threshold. Extra allowance per item eventually exceeds the fixed setup cost. questionsRewritten.cx-asymptotic-notation-q6: Replace former repetitive calculation or terse recall feedback with a self-contained conceptual walkthrough. Independently checked focus: Binary search halves the remaining sorted range, so its worst-case comparison count is logarithmic in item count n.
